summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of diastolic heart failure, chronic anticoagulation, and prior GI bleed presented with headache, chest pain, and acute anemia with a hemoglobin drop from 39 to 24.9. She was found to have a slightly elevated INR of 3.2 on Coumadin, but was hemodynamically stable. She received two units of packed red blood cells and was started on IV proton pump inhibitor therapy. Endoscopy revealed esophagitis and gastritis without active bleeding, and colonoscopy showed diverticulosis without active bleeding. Her hypoxia was attributed to mild pulmonary edema, managed with IV and oral diuretics. Her chronic chest pain persisted but was deemed non-cardiac, and headache improved without intervention. Coumadin was held initially and restarted at discharge. She was discharged home with home health services on optimized heart failure and GI protective medications, with instructions to avoid NSAIDs and monitor for rebleeding.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
